overall: The AG found the Board properly entered executive session but violated the law by not announcing all purposes; it found no violation on minutes timing or accuracy, declined the generalized claim, and ordered the audio recording released.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the July 1, 2010 executive session was illegal because the Board entered to discuss the Town Administrator's contract.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by entering into executive session on July 1, 2010.

allegations.summary: The chair announced only the contract purpose, though the executive session also covered complaints against the Town Administrator, which was not announced.
allegations.key_passage: The Chair should therefore have also cited Purpose 1, "to discuss . . . complaints or charges brought against, a public employee," at the time he announced the purpose for the executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board improperly delayed release of the July 1, 2010 executive session minutes after confidentiality purposes expired.
allegations.key_passage: From our review of the facts, it appears that the Board provided meeting minutes to the complainants within the 10 days following their requests, as required by law.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the executive session minutes were a 'complete inaccuracy' and incomplete because they did not name the individuals discussed.
Generalized claim that the executive session minutes were a 'complete inaccuracy' without specific details of the alleged violation.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review whether the minutes are a "complete inaccuracy" because we do not review generalized allegations that do not provide specific details of an alleged violation.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board unlawfully refused to publicly release the audio recording of its July 1, 2010 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Because it has been two years since the meeting, there is a new Town Administrator, and the contract negotiations have been resolved, the Board no longer has a purpose for withholding the recording under the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Publicly release the audio recording of the July 1, 2010 executive session, if not already done, subject to Public Records Law or attorney/client privilege redaction or withholding.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
